issue_context.title: MQTT causes repeated error in HA logs (paho-client) which can mean that HA stops interacting.
issue_context.body:
### The problem

This error occurs repeatedly in the logs:
```Logger: homeassistant
Source: components/mqtt/client.py:1210
First occurred: 28 June 2024 at 19:50:43 (19 occurrences)
Last logged: 05:07:00

Error doing job: Exception in callback MQTT._async_reader_callback(<paho.mqtt.cl...x7f38ca3611f0>)() (None)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/asyncio/events.py", line 88, in _run
    self._context.run(self._callback, *self._args)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/mqtt/client.py", line 577, in _async_reader_callback
    if (status := client.loop_read(MAX_PACKETS_TO_READ)) != 0:
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/paho/mqtt/client.py", line 1556, in loop_read
    rc = self._packet_read()
         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/paho/mqtt/client.py", line 2439, in _packet_read
    rc = self._packet_handle()
         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/paho/mqtt/client.py", line 3029, in _packet_handle
    return self._handle_pubackcomp("PUBACK")
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/paho/mqtt/client.py", line 3529, in _handle_pubackcomp
    rc = self._do_on_publish(mid)
         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/paho/mqtt/client.py", line 3489, in _do_on_publish
    on_publish(self, self._userdata, mid)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/mqtt/client.py", line 1210, in _async_mqtt_on_callback
    if future.done() and future.exception():
                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError: Interrupted by interrupt context manager
```
I've had issues with home assistant failing to respond across the network and the whole VM server failing.  This is the last entry in the logs

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2024.6.x

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2024.5.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

MQTT

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mqtt/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
See entry - this is a repeating entry in the logs while HA continues to run.
```


### Additional information

I have an extensive MQTT setup mainly using Zigbee2MQTT with 260 device and 2500 entities.  I've been running it for several years.  Since the latest improvements to the MQTT integration, I've started to see system instability such that HA as a whole stops interacting via its network interface or the whole server crashes.  I've reduced the frequency of this by now having a basic MQTT config (I run the latest version of eclipse-mosquitto in a container on a separate VM in the same cluster.  Before the last full system crash, there were several entries.  These included update_coordinator entries and paho-mqtt-client entries.  I've attached this log file too.  There are a couple of devices whose state causes MQTT trouble because of their length (TRVs), so I've now removed these from the setup since the last crash.  Crashing is unpredictable, and the errors at the top of the entry are still occurring, so I've raised an issue.

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>
That looks like a thread safety problem

https://community.home-assistant.io/t/2024-5-tracking-down-instability-issues-caused-by-integrations/724441

Please enable Home Assistant's debug mode and asyncio debug using the steps in 

> Using Home Assistant's built-in debug mode in 2024.5.x or later (preferred)

AND

>  Enabling asyncio debug mode at run time (preferred)
Another possibility is there is a script which does an MQTT action and get cancelled before it finishes so when the ack comes back it has no where to send it
Its also possible both problems are happening so good to check in debug mode either way

Thanks very much for your support and debugging suggestions.  I had not seen the new functions.  I don't often ask for support as I usually work it out eventually.  After I raised the issue I made 2 changes to remove entities that I thought might be triggering some of the log errors - one an entity no longer being published and the other an entity state that was too long for HA to handle.  The first of these triggered regular errors in update_coordinator.py and I suspect was the root cause.  I'm glad to say I'm not seeing any errors at all now.
